headline: Organization is putting things where you can find them—external order that supports internal clarity
universal_truth: External order supports internal order; environment shapes mind
fun_facts: The average person spends 2.5 days per year looking for lost items
Clutter has been shown to increase cortisol (stress hormone) levels
The most organized people have systems, not just clean spaces—everything has a home
discussion_questions: What does your physical space say about your mental state?
What organizing system actually works for you?
What would better organization make possible?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: Where are your keys? Your important documents? That thing you need right now? Organization isn't just tidiness—it's a system that lets you find what you need when you need it. External order creates internal peace.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: Some people seem naturally organized while others live in chaos. Is organization a personality trait you're born with, or a skill you can develop?

options.text: Organization is a skill built on systems—deciding where things go and consistently putting them there—anyone can learn it
options.response: Yes. Organized people have systems—'keys go here, bills go there.' The skill is creating and maintaining these systems. It's learnable, not innate.

options.text: Some people are just naturally better at keeping track of things
options.response: Natural tendencies vary, but organization fundamentally comes from systems, not personality...

q1.title: Everything Has a Home
q1.script: The secret of organized people: everything has a designated place. Keys go on the hook. Papers go in the file. When you finish using something, it returns home. Disorganization happens when things don't have homes—or don't go back.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "Everything Has a Home"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Clutter and Stress
q2.script: Research shows cluttered environments increase stress hormones. Visual noise competes for attention. Your brain processes everything in view. Physical clutter creates mental clutter. Cleaning your space can literally clear your mind.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Systems Over Willpower
q3.script: Organization fails when it requires constant willpower. Succeed by making organization easy: put things where they naturally land, create routines that maintain order, use systems that work with your habits rather than against them.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: External order supports internal order. Organization teaches that environment shapes mind. Create systems that work—your future self will thank you.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 186. Tomorrow, we'll explore paying attention on purpose—focus. Until then, give one homeless item in your space a permanent home.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: One Home - Reduce Finding Friction
growTrack.learning_objective: Create systems for commonly lost items
growTrack.activity: Choose one thing you frequently lose or search for. Give it a home—a specific place it always goes. Practice returning it there until it becomes automatic. One good system beats a hundred good intentions.
